forSharedLedger.detail: First pass at the raising trace. OVL18 holds 11 literal-pool references to the species table at ARM9 0x020C1374, reached by 16 LDR sites. Hand-decoding one cluster confirms the access shape: load the current creature record, read its species index, multiply by 0x84, add the table base, then load a field. That CONFIRMS THE 132-BYTE STRIDE FROM CODE rather than from the table span alone, and recovers two field offsets read by raising: +0x0C and +0x18.
forSharedLedger.confidence: +0x0C and +0x18 are hand-decoded. A wider automated scan also suggested +0x00, +0x10, +0x1C and LDRB +0x1D, which are inside the record and plausible but NOT yet hand-verified. The same scan produced +0xF8C, which is a false positive: it is outside the 132-byte record and is the global-context load that precedes the table access.
forSharedLedger.significance: The species catalog previously recorded exactly one traced read site (+0x30, on the battle path at ARM9 0x0206291C). Raising reads different fields from battle, so the record carries at least two distinct consumers. 69 of the 132 byte lanes vary across the 228 records, so most of the table is still unnamed.
forSharedLedger.nextStep: Hand-verify the four scan-only offsets, then follow each field to what OVL18 does with it. The raising FORMULAS and state machine are a separate and much larger job inside OVL18 code.

forSharedLedger.method: Hand disassembly of OVL18 read sites into the ARM9 species table at 0x020C1374, using the unpacked overlay (offset = addr - 0x0210B300) and arm9.bin (offset = addr - 0x02000000). Mapping re-verified against the known 4,8,24,60,400 control word before use.
proven: Record stride 0x84 (132) is confirmed IN CODE (MOV r0,#0x84 then MLA base+index*0x84), not merely inferred from table span / record count.
Field +0x0C: loaded, 0x1CD added, passed as the index argument to ARM9 0x0207D234 with bank 0.
Field +0x10: loaded, 0x1D4 added, passed to the SAME function with bank 0. The two base offsets differ by 7.

ARM9 0x0207D234 is a two-level resource accessor: ADD r0,r0,r0,LSL#4 then LDR [r2, r0 LSL#4] selects a table at a 272-byte stride by bank, then LDR [r0, r1 LSL#2] indexes it by word. It returns a pointer, which OVL18 stores into the raising context.

Field +0x18 is a BITMASK. The code runs the lowest-set-bit idiom (MVN / SUB #1 / AND) then RSB r0,#0x20 to turn it into a position, then adds 1 - so it is converted to a 1-based ordinal rather than used as a number.
forSharedLedger.corrected: The earlier automated pass reported a read at +0x1C. That was a FALSE POSITIVE: at 0x2125f24 the +0x1c load is from r9, an unrelated base, while the species-table load at that site is +0x0C. Also previously rejected: +0xF8C, which is outside the 132-byte record.

forSharedLedger.summary: The species record at ARM9 0x020C1374 (228 records, stride 0x84) now has four identity fields resolved by combining hand disassembly of the OVL18 read sites with a read of the actual values across all 228 records.

fields.meaning: pointer to a NUL-terminated ASCII species identifier
fields.evidence: DATA_VERIFIED: all 228 pointers land inside the ARM9 image and all 228 targets are NUL-terminated ASCII of length >= 3. Record 0 is the egg identifier.

CODE + DATA: 7 distinct values 0..6 across the table; OVL18 adds 0x1CD and calls the bank-0 resource accessor, i.e. it indexes a text block. 7 matches the documented stages (egg plus the six growth stages).
CODE + DATA: 5 distinct values 0..4; OVL18 adds 0x1D4 and calls the SAME accessor. 5 matches Vaccine/Virus/Data/Free plus a none for the stages help entry 119 says have no attribute.

CODE + DATA: the only values present are 0 and the eight single bits 0x01..0x80, and OVL18 runs the lowest-set-bit idiom then RSB #0x20 and +1 to turn it into a 1-based ordinal. Eight bits matches the eight families help entry 120 documents.

forSharedLedger.internalCrosscheck: 0x1D4 - 0x1CD = 7, exactly the number of distinct generation values. The generation and attribute strings are therefore adjacent blocks in one bank-0 table, which is what two indices seven apart into the same accessor implied.
forSharedLedger.boundaryCrosscheck: Records 0..7 carry family 0 and generation 0, matching the documented split of 224 = 8 eggs + 216 regular entities.
forSharedLedger.stillUnknown: +0x1D is a byte with 7 distinct values in 12..32 and is not yet interpreted. forSharedLedger.method: Rewrote the field scanner to be dataflow-confirmed: a load only counts as a field read if its base register genuinely derives from the table base through a multiply by 0x84, and any offset >= 0x84 is discarded. The two earlier passes each produced a false positive (+0xF8C, +0x1C-from-r9); this pass produced none.
forSharedLedger.scanResult: Six field reads across all modules: +0x04 (arm9), +0x0C (arm9, ovl0, ovl16, ovl18), +0x10 (arm9, ovl16, ovl18), +0x18 (arm9, ovl16, ovl18), +0x1C byte (ovl0), +0x70 byte (ovl0).

newlyResolved.finding: Pointer to a second ASCII string used as a LOOKUP KEY. ARM9 0x02097A0C walks the table calling 0x0201FFC0 with (key, needle, 4) and captures the record index when the result is zero. 0x0201FFC0 was disassembled and is byte-wise compare: returns the difference on mismatch, stops at NUL, counts down the length - strncmp. The first four characters are as discriminating as the whole string, giving 224 distinct prefixes across 228 records.
Byte read by Hunt. FULLY DETERMINED BY GENERATION with zero violations across all 228 records: 0->1, 1->6, 2->8, 3->10, 4->14, 5->18, 6->24.

forSharedLedger.question: The Owner challenged the claim that the original has a care loop, noting it did not look like it. The challenge was fair: the previous claim rested on the game HELP TEXT describing hunger, sickness, injury and permanent loss, plus the tool vocabulary, and NOT on any evidence that the code runs those mechanics. forSharedLedger.method: Scanned OVL18 for read-modify-write on struct fields - a simulation must WRITE state - then disassembled one site by hand.
proven: OVL18 contains 100 read-modify-write sites on struct fields. It is a simulation, not a menu shell.

Field +0x1C of the creature record is a CLAMPED 0..100 METER. At OVL18 0x021186E8 the code loads it, adds 0x32 (50), stores it, reloads, compares against 0x64 (100) and stores the clamp when it is over. Cap and restore step are both explicit constants.
The same field is decremented elsewhere in the same overlay: SUB #10, SUB #2 and SUB #1 sites exist, alongside ADD #3 and ADD #1.
The restore at 0x021186E8 is guarded: the code first loads another field and executes only when that value is <= 0.
forSharedLedger.stillUnknown: WHICH meter +0x1C is. Nothing here names it hunger, and no time-driven decrement has been isolated yet - the SUB sites are at specific code sites whose trigger is untraced. So "the original maintains per-creature clamped meters with restore and drain" is now proven; "not feeding a Digimon eventually kills it" is not.
forSharedLedger.processChange: The Owner set a standing rule on 2026-09-04: before starting work on any part, confirm which evidence tier it sits at, and specifically whether the BEHAVIOUR is verified rather than only documented. Adopted.

proven: OVL18 0x02111130 populates two slots side by side: +0x114 from the incoming argument, then it reads that record field +0x00 as a species index, does MOV #0x84 / MLA against the species table base, and stores the result at +0x118. So +0x114 is the CREATURE record and +0x118 is its SPECIES record, proven by construction rather than inferred.
At OVL18 0x021187E0 the penalty is conditional: threshold = species[+0x1C]; if creature[+0x08] >= threshold then creature[+0x1C] -= 10.
At OVL18 0x021186E8 the same meter is restored: creature[+0x1C] += 50, then reloaded, compared against 100 and clamped. Cap and step are explicit constants.
creature[+0x08] is incremented by 1 nearby (0x02118730), in the same handler as the restore and the penalty.
forSharedLedger.correction: The species byte at +0x1C was previously recorded as a memory-card capacity CANDIDATE, reasoning from help entry 128 that capacity rises on evolution. That reading is withdrawn. It is a THRESHOLD in a comparison, not a cost drawn from a pool. It was transcribed under the neutral name generationScaledByte and never shipped as capacity, so no product behaviour depended on the wrong reading.
forSharedLedger.meaning: The original does maintain a per-creature clamped 0..100 meter with a restore step, a penalty step, an accumulating counter, and a per-generation threshold that decides when the penalty applies. Higher generations tolerate a larger counter before being penalised.
forSharedLedger.stillUnknown: What the meter and the counter MEASURE, and what drives the counter upward. Until the increment trigger is traced it is not established whether this is time pressure or a cost attached to specific actions - and those imply different products.

proven: The meter handler at OVL18 0x0211837C has ZERO direct BL callers. It is reached through a dispatch table, the same shape the battle lane found for its state machine.
That table is at OVL18 0x021283D0 .. 0x02128968: 180 entries, 8-byte stride laid out as {handler pointer, 0}, and all 180 pointers are distinct. The meter handler is index 96.

Inside the handler the accumulation is indexed: creature+0x100 is an ARRAY of halfwords; the code does accumulator[r4] += r4, and only when that accumulator reaches 4 or more does creature+0x08 increment. So the rate is driven by the index r4, and the meter penalty is two thresholds deep, not one.
forSharedLedger.chainNowTraced: accumulator[r4] += r4  ->  at >= 4, creature[+0x08] += 1  ->  at creature[+0x08] >= species[+0x1C] (per-generation threshold), creature[+0x1C] -= 10, against a meter restored in +50 steps and clamped at 100.
forSharedLedger.forkStillOpen: Whether this is time pressure or an action cost still hinges on what selects handler index 96 and what r4 is. Both now have a precise address to work from rather than a guess. This is where the stage ends; closing the fork is the next stage, not a step within this one.
forSharedLedger.productImpact: NOTHING was implemented from any of this. No care system, no meter, no threshold has been added to the product, because the trigger is not established and the Owner rule adopted 2026-09-04 is to confirm behaviour before building.

forSharedLedger.correction: The claim "180-entry handler table, meter handler at index 96" is WITHDRAWN. That came from walking outward from a known entry while the {pointer, 0} pattern held, which ran straight through the end of one table and into the next.
forSharedLedger.proven: OVL18 0x02110C38 reads a global at +0xA8 and tests it against 1, 3 and 5. On a match it registers the table at 0x021283D0 with size 0x260 (76 entries); otherwise it registers 0x02128630 with size 0x340 (104 entries). Both sizes are explicit MOV immediates at the registration calls, so the bounds are stated by the code rather than inferred from data shape.
forSharedLedger.revised: The meter handler entry at 0x021286D0 lies inside the SECOND set: index 20 of 104, active when the global mode at +0xA8 is not 1, 3 or 5.
forSharedLedger.meaning: Dispatch is mode-gated. Which handler set is live depends on a global mode selector, which is the same +0xA8 the battle lane already found deciding a one-entry match mode. So the raising handlers are not a flat list; there are at least two sets and the mode chooses.
forSharedLedger.stillOpen: What mode values 1/3/5 mean, and what selects index 20 within the active set. The fork - time pressure versus action cost - is still not closed, and nothing has been implemented from any of it.

forSharedLedger.toolWarning: WITHDRAWN AND CORRECTED 2026-09-04. The claim that the literal-pool matcher produced a fourth false positive was WRONG. The words at OVL12 0x0210E450 and 0x0210D000 are 0xE59F1088, genuine LDR Rt,[pc,#imm] instructions; the matcher identified them correctly. The real mistake was mine: the scratch disassembler was bound to arm9_overlay_0018.bin and I fed it OVL12 addresses. Overlays share the RAM base 0x0210B300, so the offsets resolved without error and produced confident-looking output from the wrong binary.
forSharedLedger.productImpact: Nothing implemented. Gate entrance fee and rank gating remain unbuilt, as they were before this round.
forSharedLedger.rootCauseReview: Reviewing the four incidents, they had FOUR DIFFERENT causes, not one unreliable tool: (1) species +0xF8C was a missing bounds check, since 0xF8C exceeds the 0x84 record - fixed by rejecting offsets >= stride; (2) the +0x1C-from-r9 hit was loose dataflow in the first scanner - fixed by the stricter version that requires derivation through a multiply by the stride; (3) the 180-entry table was a greedy outward walk running through the end of one table into the next - a method error, fixed by reading the size the registration code passes; (4) this one was wrong-overlay disassembly, a process error with no tool defect at all. Calling them all one broken matcher was itself a wrong diagnosis.
forSharedLedger.actualFix: Not a rewrite. The disassembler needs the overlay id passed explicitly and should refuse an address whose overlay is not the one loaded, so the same mix-up fails loudly instead of printing plausible instructions.
forSharedLedger.newFinding: With the correct overlay, both sites read cleanly: OVL12 0x0210E450 does LDRH from table base+24 indexed by the record offset, and 0x0210D000 does LDRSH - SIGNED - from base+26. A fee would not be signed, so base+24 is the stronger entrance-fee candidate and base+26 is something that can go negative.

forSharedLedger.proven: OVL12 0x0210E450 loads the literal at 0x0210E4E0, which holds 0x020C9570 - the gate table base plus 24 - and does LDRH from it indexed by the record offset, so the field is an UNSIGNED u16 at record+0x18. It passes the value to 0x0210E588, which offsets a UI object, sets r3 to 7, loads a format literal and calls 0x0207F958. A width of 7 matches the seven-digit money display the footage shows.
forSharedLedger.alsoProven: The neighbouring field at record+0x1A is read with LDRSH at OVL12 0x0210D000 - SIGNED - so it can go negative and is therefore not money.
forSharedLedger.notProven: That record+0x18 IS the entrance fee. It is a per-gate value drawn as a 7-digit number, which is consistent with a fee and rules out the signed neighbour, but no comparison against player funds and no deduction has been traced. The values across the 17 records are 0, 364, 50, 230, 0, 308, 66, 574, 744, 110, 816, 216, 1350, 108, 2608, 4320, 0.
forSharedLedger.weakSupport: Record 0 carries 0 and the footage shows one gate at an entrance fee of 0, but no gate name is mapped to a record index, so this is a coincidence of shape rather than a match.
forSharedLedger.nextStep: Find the site that compares this field against the player funds, or that deducts it. That is what would make it the fee rather than a number that happens to be drawn like money.

forSharedLedger.proven: ARM9 0x02089230 is the game's own what-is-on-today query. It asks the clock for season and day, then walks the 62-record table at 0x020CD004 at stride 0x28 matching field14 against the season and field18 against the day, with a third condition comparing field10 against HALF a u16 at player+0x0AE8. It emits record indices, its scan bound is 0x3D so record 61 is never reached, and its capacity check guards the store rather than the loop.
forSharedLedger.alsoProven: The two string columns are two parallel 62-entry blocks in nitrofs/ui/txt/txt_list_txt.dat: field00 runs 675..736 and field04 runs 737..798, with field04 minus field00 equal to 62 for every record. Record 61, the one the scan bound excludes, is the tutorial match -- which is why it is not a fixture.
forSharedLedger.notProven: What the counter at player+0x0AE8 counts. field10 only holds 0..4 so a counter of 8 clears everything, but there is no traced write site. The board therefore shows the whole calendar and marks the threshold rather than hiding rows behind it. field0C, field1C, field20 and field24 keep their byte-offset names.
forSharedLedger.languageNote: The cartridge is the Japanese YDIJ release, so the fixture names are Japanese. The research footage is the English release, a different build; its labels are not evidence for this ROM's string table, and no translation was invented.

forSharedLedger.what: The first build of the string catalog shipped blurbs still holding the bank's two-character backslash-n instead of real line breaks, so the board rendered the escape as visible text. Caught by looking at the live page, not by the tests, which had not asserted it.
forSharedLedger.cause: The builder's comparison had been written as a real newline rather than the two literal characters -- the backslash was un-escaped on its way into the file.
forSharedLedger.fix: The value is now a named constant spelled chr(92) + n, which cannot be mangled the same way, and a regression test asserts that all 62 blurbs carry real breaks and no residual escape.

forSharedLedger.proven: help_text_txt.dat declares 168 entries and they are two parallel blocks of 84: entry i is a title, entry i+84 is its body. The offset is fixed by a control this project already relied on -- entry 96, previously cited for the clock cascade, lands on the TIME title under this split. Sixteen bodies are the literal string n/a; those titles are section headings. The remaining 68 are topics. The heading/topic split is the file's, not a reading of the Japanese.
forSharedLedger.correction: The figure of 170 help strings used in earlier discussion was wrong. The bank holds 168 entries, which is 84 titles and 84 bodies, so there are 68 readable topics -- not 170 paragraphs.
forSharedLedger.notProven: Which heading owns which topics. The bank stores headings and topics as separate runs with no parent link, and no grouping table was found in ARM9, OVL5 (help resource descriptor) or OVL16 (loader pointer). The screen therefore renders the ROM's own order and asserts no tree; a test forbids any record from carrying a parent field while this stays untraced.
forSharedLedger.alsoRecorded: The help overlays are OVL5 and OVL16. An earlier scan of mine mislabelled every overlay as ovl9 because the id was taken with a regex that matched the 9 in the arm9 filename prefix; the corrected scan is what produced OVL5/OVL16.

forSharedLedger.proven: tamer_info_main_scene.nxr and tamer_info_sub_scene.nxr (both OVL4) name every field on the screen, and because the cartridge draws each digit as its own sprite-cell node the node names also fix the widths: title 3, guid 3, map 3, battle 4, win 3 on the main scene; money 7, time 3 plus a separator plus 2, have 3 on the sub scene. Row order follows the scene y positions 22/44/66/109/131 and 72/113/154.
forSharedLedger.crossCheck: The 7-digit money field now has three independent ROM witnesses: the sub scene lays out money0..money6, the battle reward path clamps the wallet at 9999999, and the gate draw call at OVL12 0x0210E588 passes a field width of 7 to the number renderer. A test asserts the first two agree.

Those are lifetime counters the cartridge keeps in its save and this build has no traced read site for any of them. ruledOut.what: The byte cluster at +0x1A8..+0x1B4, which a store-frequency scan of OVL18 surfaced as five consecutive byte fields -- exactly the shape of five raising stats.
ruledOut.why: OVL18 0x02119BB0 reads +0x1A8, compares against 4 and jumps through a five-entry table. Phase 0 sets a 32-bit timer at +0x1AC to 0x3000, writes 31 to +0x1B0, zeroes +0x1B1 and +0x1B4, and calls ARM9 0x020472CC twice -- which is nothing but STRB r1,[r0,#0x15]; BX lr, a generic byte setter. Phase 1 copies three consecutive words into +0xF8/+0xFC/+0x100, an x/y/z position. This is an actor animation controller, not persistent creature state.
ruledOut.value: This was the most tempting wrong answer available and would have produced invented 'raising numbers' that looked ROM-derived.

forSharedLedger.alsoRuledOut: 0x50 appeared 11 times before a MUL and looked like an 80-byte creature record stride. At 0x02113480 it is arithmetic instead -- the product is shifted right by 5, the signed divide-by-32 idiom, so the site computes x * 80 / 32. Not a stride.
forSharedLedger.structuralFinding: The raising stats are NOT at fixed offsets from the player structure. Every immediate offset in the 0x400..0xF00 window across OVL18 was tallied; the hot fields (+0x404..+0x44C, +0x6DC, +0xB18, +0xDFC, +0xE28) are word-sized and pointer-shaped, not stat bytes. The three known save fields (Bits +0x4C8, tamer rank +0xAE8, gate waiver +0xEB8) are fixed, but creature records are reached through a pointer, which is why an offset scan cannot find them.
forSharedLedger.toolCheck: Suspected my disassembler was misprinting MUL operands; decoded the raw word by hand and it is correct. No tool defect.

forSharedLedger.withdrawn: speciesBaseStats.js claimed the stat curve CANNOT be the source of attack, defence, wisdom and speed, because columns 1..6 are byte-identical and would emit one number under four labels. The observation was right; the premise was wrong. WITHDRAWN.
forSharedLedger.proven: ARM9 0x02062900 builds a creature instance. For every stat it repeats one shape: LDR the stat's OWN index out of the source record, MOV it LSL #4 (the 16-byte row stride), LDRH from that stat's own column pointer, STR the value onto the instance. The seven column pointers sit in one literal pool as consecutive +2 offsets from 0x020CA008 -- 008, 00A, 00C, 00E, 010, 012, 014 -- which is what proves they are columns of one table rather than seven tables. The rung is also copied to the instance at +0x84, +0x88, +0x8C, +0x90, +0x94, +0x98.
forSharedLedger.model: The curve is a LADDER of 27 rungs. Column 0 is HP: 200, 280, ... 7000. Columns 1..6 are one shared ladder: 10, 14, ... 350. Two stats differ not by which column they read but by which rung they stand on, so identical columns are the design and not a defect.
forSharedLedger.alsoProven: The per-creature record stride is 0x44 (68 bytes), from OVL10 0x021100E0 (MOV r1,#0x44; MLA r2,r0,r1,r5). The stat rungs are fields inside it at +0x14, +0x18, +0x1C, +0x20, +0x24, +0x28, +0x2C, +0x30 and onward.
forSharedLedger.consequence: The long-standing 'four stats have no source' gap has a correct answer at last: they were never species constants. A species does not have an attack value; a CREATURE has an attack rung, and training is what moves it. That also names what Phase 4 has to find -- the magnitude by which a training session advances a rung.
forSharedLedger.notShippable: The rungs are save state, not a ROM table, so there is nothing to transcribe yet. statLadder.js exposes the ladder and refuses to guess where any creature stands on it; CREATURE_RECORD_RUNG_EVIDENCE stays UNKNOWN_REQUIRES_TRACE and a test enforces that.

forSharedLedger.raisedBy: Claude Code, from an Owner-supplied DeSmuME save state
forSharedLedger.method: The DeSmuME .ds1 save state is a zlib stream after a 32-byte header. Inflating gives 11,167,748 bytes; main RAM was located inside it by searching for the clock cascade fingerprint (4,8,24,60,400 as LE u32, which must sit at 0x020C8A4C) and then VERIFIED by matching a 512-byte chunk of arm9.bin at the implied base. Extraction is reproducible from any future save state by the same two steps.

confirmed.playerStruct: The global at 0x020FBA08 -> +0x04 chain resolves on live memory to player base 0x021C24C0. All three known offsets read correctly: +0x4C8 Bits = 10000, +0xAE8 tamer rank = 0, +0xEB8 gate waiver = 0. The gate-fee trace and the tamer-rank identification are now confirmed against a running game, not only against static code.
confirmed.statLadder: A live creature instance sits at 0x021C31E8 with HP 360 and TP 14, each duplicated into a pair of fields (0x50/0x58 and 0x54/0x5C). 360 is exactly HP-ladder rung 2 and 14 is exactly shared-ladder rung 1. The ladder is therefore the real source of base stats, confirmed on live data rather than inferred from a disassembly.

forSharedLedger.notConfirmed: The exact rung-to-value pairing beyond the first stat. The instance holds nine stat values at +0x60..+0x80 (18,19,19,19,10,10,11,11,10) and nine small numbers at +0x84..+0xA4 (2,2,2,2,3,0,1,1,1). The first pair matches the ladder exactly (rung 2 -> 18) but three others sit exactly ONE above their predicted ladder value and one is far off. Off-by-one across several stats reads like a modifier applied after the build rather than a wrong model, but that is a hypothesis and is not asserted.
forSharedLedger.nextStep: A second capture taken after a single feeding, diffed against this one, would name the changed fields directly. The persistent 68-byte record (stride 0x44, from OVL10 0x021100E0) has not yet been located in RAM; the instance at 0x021C31E8 is the built copy, not the stored one.

forSharedLedger.raisedBy: Claude Code, from an Owner-supplied before/after save-state pair
forSharedLedger.method: Slots ds1 (08:41) and ds2 (08:42) are one minute apart in the same session, and both resolve to the SAME player base 0x021C24A0, so an absolute byte diff is valid with no realignment. Across 4 MB only 5,703 bytes differ, and inside the player structure only 11 runs.
forSharedLedger.methodWarning: An earlier pair from different sessions had the player base move from 0x021C24C0 to 0x021C24A0. A naive absolute diff across sessions is worthless; always confirm the base matches, and align to it when it does not.
forSharedLedger.finding: Feeding does NOT immediately change a hunger value. What changes is object bookkeeping: two pointers (0x022857E8 and 0x022F24C0) move from player+0x3814/+0x3868 to player+0x3878/+0x38CC, and three slots flip from 0 to 1 at player+0x3E20, +0x40A0 and +0x4240. That is a food object being spawned and queued, which matches the cartridge's own help text -- feeding PLACES food in the cage and the Digimon eats it over time.
forSharedLedger.consequence: The raising state does not move when the tool is used; it moves when the creature acts or the day advances. A capture pair for the hunger field has to span TIME PASSING or an END_DAY, not a tool press. This corrects the capture protocol.
forSharedLedger.alsoClarified: The creature instance found in the 2026-09-04 capture (HP 360, TP 14, ladder rungs) was a BATTLE instance -- that capture was taken during a battle. Neither ranch capture contains one, which confirms ARM9 0x02062900 builds a combat-time copy rather than the persistent record. The persistent 68-byte record is still unlocated.
forSharedLedger.unexplained: A regular array at 0x020F2324 with stride 0x24 shows single-byte changes in the 13..33 range across at least 15 entries. Shape and value range read like per-actor animation state, but it is not identified and is not claimed.

forSharedLedger.raisedBy: Claude Code, with an Owner correction that fixed the search
forSharedLedger.correction: An earlier note called the 2026-09-04 instance a BATTLE copy because a screenshot showed an explosion. The Owner corrected this: there was no battle, that was FIELD TRAINING (running), which spends current HP and raises maximum HP. The instance is the ranch creature itself.
forSharedLedger.searchBug: That correction also exposed a defect in my own fingerprint. It required current HP == max HP (+0x50 equal to +0x58), which only holds for an untrained creature. Once the Owner trained, current fell below max and the search returned zero -- I had read that as 'no creature present' when it meant 'my filter excluded it'. Relaxing to current <= max, and restricting to the heap above the ARM9 image, found it immediately.
forSharedLedger.located: The live creature record sits at 0x02130714, with a second copy at 0x021E7F84. Across the feeding pair: HP 47/360 -> 105/360, TP 10/10 unchanged.
forSharedLedger.ladderConfirmedAgain: Max HP 360 is exactly HP-ladder rung 2 and max TP 10 is exactly shared-ladder rung 0. That is a third independent confirmation of the ladder model, this time on a ranch creature rather than a trained one.
forSharedLedger.notProven: Whether the +58 HP is the feeding or ordinary regeneration over the 62 seconds between captures. One capture pair cannot separate them; a pair with the same interval and NO feeding would.
forSharedLedger.openDetail: The stat values at +0x60..+0x74 read 10,14,10,10,10,11 while the indices at +0x84..+0x98 read 0,0,0,0,1,0. The 11 is not a ladder value at all (the ladder runs 10,14,18,22), so a modifier is applied on top of the ladder base. Consistent with the off-by-one seen in the 2026-09-04 capture, still not explained.

forSharedLedger.raisedBy: Claude Code, from four Owner save states spanning an evolution
forSharedLedger.proven: Evolution does not modify the creature record in place. It DESTROYS the old one and allocates a new one. Across four states in one session (player base constant at 0x021C24A0): ds1/ds2 hold a record at 0x02130714 with HP 47/360 then 105/360; ds3, taken mid-evolution, has that address fully zeroed and no record matching anywhere in the heap; ds4 has a new record at 0x02131BB0 with HP 200/200.
forSharedLedger.alsoObserved: The new record starts at FULL HP, and its max HP of 200 is ladder rung 0 -- the bottom of the ladder -- where the old record's 360 was rung 2. The first words also shift by one slot: the old record opened 14, 0, 6 and the new one opens 10, 14, 0, which reads like a history chain pushing the new form to the front.
forSharedLedger.notProven: Which field holds the species. The on-screen message said the creature evolved into KOROMON, which is species index 21, but neither record carries 21 in its opening fields (they hold 14 and 10, which are BOTAMON and NYOKIMON). Either the opening words are not species ids, or these records are not the creature the message named, or the visible evolution happened later than ds4. Not resolved, and not guessed.
forSharedLedger.alsoNotProven: Whether max HP genuinely FALLS on evolution. A drop from rung 2 to rung 0 is counter-intuitive and has at least two innocent explanations, so the observation is recorded and the conclusion is not.
forSharedLedger.nextStep: The watcher script (watch.lua) settles all of this: it logs every changed offset with a frame number, so the evolution transition names its own fields instead of being inferred from four snapshots. It has not been run yet.
forSharedLedger.toolNote: Screen capture of the emulator now works through occlusion via PrintWindow with PW_RENDERFULLCONTENT, so the game can be observed without disturbing the Owner's foreground window. Confirmed against a live frame showing the status bar as Spring | 3-day | ikusei | 12:30, which matches the four-field info_bar layout this project built from the ROM scene.

forSharedLedger.raisedBy: Claude Code, from an Owner-recorded video of the running game
forSharedLedger.tier: LIVE_FOOTAGE_OBSERVATION -- the Owner recorded the Japanese cartridge running in DeSmuME, so this is the right build and the right language, but it is one observed instance and not a traced formula.
forSharedLedger.training: The game states its own training result in text: 'あいうえおはHPが90あがった' followed by 'かしこさがさがった' -- HP rose by 90 AND wisdom fell. Training is therefore a TRADE, not a pure gain. The status panel in the same frame reads HP 238/480, TP 15/15, capacity 12 G, on Spring day 5 at 08:50.
forSharedLedger.maxHpIsNotALadderValue: 480 is not a rung of the HP ladder (200, 280, 360, 440, 520...). Neither is the implied previous value of 390. So maximum HP is NOT constrained to ladder values: the ladder supplies a base and training adds on top of it. That finally explains the anomaly seen in two memory captures, where stat values sat exactly one above their predicted rung.
forSharedLedger.feeding: Feeding consumes an inventory item and the game reports the remaining count: 'エサのこり45コ', then 44, then 43 across three feeds. This matches the memory diff, which showed object bookkeeping (pointers moving between lists, slots flipping 0 to 1) rather than an instant stat change.
forSharedLedger.correction: The HP recovery seen earlier (47 -> 105 across the feeding pair) was NOT feeding and NOT idle regeneration. The Owner identified it as the effect of a HEALING CAGE the creature was standing in. That is the cage-effect magnitude which cageEffects.js currently flags as UNKNOWN_REQUIRES_TRACE, so the observation lands directly on an open item.
forSharedLedger.alsoSeen: An evolution sequence, with the lower screen showing the EVOLUTION presentation.
forSharedLedger.whatThisDoesNotGive: The formulas. +90 is one sample from one creature at one moment; the rule that produced it, and what determines which stat falls, still have to come from the code. The value of this footage is that it names WHAT to look for -- a paired raise/lower on training, an item decrement on feeding, and a cage-driven HP restore.

forSharedLedger.raisedBy: Claude Code, from an anchor the Owner supplied by video
forSharedLedger.howItStarted: The Owner's recording showed the game printing its own training result. Searching the text bank for those words found the format templates: entry 1 is '[5]は[3]が[4]あがった' and entry 2 is '[3]が[4]さがった'. A template with a stat-name slot implies a stat-name table, and that table is what the search then found.
forSharedLedger.statOrder: Entries 35..40 are the six stat labels in the game's own order: HP, TP, KOUGEKI (attack), BOUGYO (defence), KASHIKOSA (wisdom), SUBAYASA (speed). The training messages substitute from this list, so this IS the canonical stat order -- the thing the raising lane has needed all along to say which field is which.
forSharedLedger.alsoRecovered: Entries 20..29 are ten family names and 30..34 are five resistances (heat, cold, thunder, light, dark), the last matching help topic 42's statement that there are five attack types.
forSharedLedger.speciesNames: A run of Digimon names begins at entry 41 and maps to the species table at a constant offset of 33, covering species 8..223 -- exactly 216 entries. Species 0..7 are eggs with no individual name; 224..227 fall past the run onto the name-entry kana charts.
forSharedLedger.corroboration: The run being exactly 216 long is independently witnessed by databaseCatalog.js, which records the encyclopedia as 224 slots = 8 eggs + 216 regular. Those two facts were derived years apart in this project by unrelated means and agree exactly.
forSharedLedger.guardDesign: The Japanese-character check alone does NOT pin the offset -- +32 also passes it, because a shifted run is still Japanese. What pins it is a control drawn from the cartridge's own screen output: species 21 must be KOROMON. Both +32 and +34 fail that. The coarse filter and the precise control do different jobs and both are kept.
forSharedLedger.shipped: The names now reach the roster: projectRoster carries speciesName and the Digimon screen shows a SPECIES row. Eggs and the four unnamed species render as absent rather than blank.

forSharedLedger.raisedBy: Claude Code, prompted by the Owner asking what each cage does
forSharedLedger.defect: cageEffects.js carried a hand-entered per-cage channel and capacity that was OFF BY ONE against the cartridge for all 36 records. It opened with 'Defense up, best for 2' -- a cage that does not exist in the ROM -- which pushed every real cage down one slot. It also recorded definition 35 as the Waiting Room; 34 is the waiting room and 35 is FUTA, the lid.
forSharedLedger.impact: Every cage in the running build showed the wrong effect and the wrong recommended occupancy. Cage choice is the main raising decision, so the product was misreporting the whole mechanic.
forSharedLedger.nowCorrect: Definition 0 is UNDOUJOU, a running track: HP up, best for 6. 1 is the stadium (speed, 10), 2 the dojo (TP, 6), 3 the gym (attack, 8), 22 the temple (wisdom, 2), 14 the mini infirmary (HP and stress recover, 2).
forSharedLedger.confirmedOnScreen: The Owner photographed the cartridge's own cage shop. MINI-GYM reads 'gym mini version / attack up / best for 2' and is definition 29; MINI-INFIRMARY reads 'HP stress recover / best for 2' and is definition 14. Both match the transcription word for word, from a source independent of the ROM read.
forSharedLedger.alsoFound: NO cage trains defence. BOUGYO is a real stat -- fourth in the game's own stat list -- but no cage description names it. The DEFENSE channel was the fabricated entry that started the off-by-one, and a test now asserts it stays unused.
forSharedLedger.stillOpen: Magnitudes. The cartridge states WHICH stat each cage moves and the recommended occupancy, but never how much a tick moves it. A guess that record columns +0x10..+0x24 were six per-stat magnitudes was tested and REFUTED -- the speed cage carries zero in the speed slot -- and that refutation is recorded in the builder so it is not retried.

There was no design reason: the gate world got wired during VS2 and battle_menu/launcher13.nsbmd sat in the art registry marked NEEDS_REBUILD and was never picked up. forSharedLedger.romEvidence: launcher13.nsbmd's node table proves both shape and face set: a `box` node with _00_edge and _01_edgelight trim, then _02_champ, _03_title, _04_free and _05_tushin, each with bg/l/u variants. The four names line up with the battle kinds help topics 69-74 list.
forSharedLedger.keyRealisation: The Gate world in production is NOT the ROM model -- its manifest reads 'Procedural high-resolution world sphere with original-created vertex colours'. The cartridge model supplies STRUCTURE and the product builds its own geometry. So the box needed no art-lane conversion and could be built immediately under the same clean-room policy.
forSharedLedger.structuralFinding: The box selects a battle KIND, not a match. The original has two layers -- kind, then match within it -- and this build had collapsed them into one flat match list. The box is now drawn with all four faces disabled and an on-screen note, because which matches belong to which kind is NOT traced. No face pretends to lead anywhere.

Both were caught by existing guards, both are fixed: styles moved to vs5Styles.css, and the box now draws on demand exactly as the Gate sphere does.
